note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. 28 rows = 14 items x resp {0,1}; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets exactly. (1) STEP 3b, identity checked not assumed: the deposit's only WI block is the 14 columns WI_1..WI_14, every one binary, and each live wi_n column-sum reproduces its raw WI_n sum exactly (49,21,49,48,14,45,19,28,15,25,34,43,24,51 over n=83) -- so the table is the 14-item Whiteley Index and not one of the deposit's other instruments (CSS-15, PANAS 20, four symptom-concern items at two waves, all separate IRW tables). (2) CODE DERIVATION: number-preserving rename, WI_n -> wi_n (lowercase). No positional step. (3) BUT the source grants no text: the .xlsx header row carries bare codes only, there are no variable or value labels anywhere in the file (it is a plain spreadsheet), the deposit holds no other file, and the figshare record lists no linked publication or related material -- the journal article was not locatable as of 2026-09-16. So WHICH canonical Whiteley item each number is rests on the instrument's own published numbering, not on anything in this dataset; mapping_basis=paper_order, verification PARTIAL (see verify_wolters2026_wi.R): item-rest correlations track Axelsson et al.'s published per-item loadings at Spearman 0.54, permutation p=0.026 over 20,000 draws, which rules out a permutation of the item text but does not separate items of similar loading (wi_8/wi_13 both 0.68; wi_10 0.58 vs wi_11 0.60). (4) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered in German -- German funder (BMUV), University of Cologne authors, and the deposit's own education categories are translated German school qualifications ('lower secondary school certificate', 'university entrance qualification'). No German wording exists in the deposit or in any paper supplement (there is no supplement), so the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: English in the base fields, empty _translated columns, language=German, text_source=translated_substitute. (5) translation_source=third_party_english, not official_instrument_english: Pilowsky (1967) is closed access, so the English shipped is Eslami et al.'s Table 1 reproduction, transcribed verbatim including its '(through the radio, television, newspapers or someone you know)' parenthesis and its plural 'very serious illnesses'. One known divergence from the instrument original: Eslami's item 2 reads 'many aches and pains' where Axelsson et al.'s descriptor for #2 is 'Bothered by many pains and aches'; the shipped wording is Eslami's, unaltered. No other deviation from that table. (6) OPTION TEXT IS FLIPPED ON wi_9, deliberately. The deposit stores Whiteley SCORES rather than raw answers: item 9 ('Is it easy for you to forget about yourself...') is the scale's single reverse-keyed item, and its item-rest correlation in the live data is +0.32 (n=83, p~0.003), where raw yes/no storage would make it clearly negative; only 15 of 83 score 1, i.e. 82% gave the low-health-anxiety answer, which is what a general sample does. So wi_9 ships Yes=0 / No=1 and the other thirteen ship No=0 / Yes=1. Same move as burkert_2019_whoqol_bref and wang_2016_study1_se, recorded rather than made silently; irw-validate may flag resp_ambiguous on this table and that flag is correct about it. (7) instructions and section_prompt blank: no instruction stem is published in the deposit and none was invented. section_id is the trivial wolters2026_wi_1; correct_response blank throughout (no correct answer). (8) RIGHTS: no block. The Whiteley Index has no row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be located or quoted for it: there is no rights-holder terms page, the scale is reproduced in full in open-access validation papers (Eslami et al. 2017, CC BY), and the 1967 Br J Psychiatry article carries only the journal's own copyright notice, which is a notice about the article rather than a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). Shipped under 'silence is permission'; per the standing rule a round may not write a ship row, so no register row was added. The source actually copied from (Russian Open Medical Journal) is itself open access.
public_note: Item wording for this table is shown in English: the study was run in German and no German wording is published in its figshare deposit (a plain spreadsheet whose only WI content is the column names WI_1..WI_14), so the Whiteley Index's English, as reproduced by Eslami, Ahmadipour & Bagheri (2017), ships instead. Two things to read carefully. Which of the fourteen canonical Whiteley items each code wi_1..wi_14 refers to is inferred from the instrument's own numbering, not stated by the source: the item-rest profile matches published per-item loadings at Spearman 0.54 (permutation p = 0.026), which rules out a scrambled mapping but would not detect a swap between two items of similar loading. And the responses are Whiteley SCORES, not raw answers, so for wi_9 -- the scale's one reverse-keyed item -- a 1 means the respondent answered 'no', the opposite of every other item; its item-rest correlation is +0.32 where raw storage would be negative.
